test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 28 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What happens when a pendulum bob swings from its mean position to extreme position?

options.text: Both kinetic and potential energies increase
Potential energy decreases, kinetic energy increases
Potential energy increases, kinetic energy decreases

solution: The correct answer is __**Potential energy increases, kinetic energy decreases**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • When the pendulum bob swings from its **mean position** (equilibrium point) to the **extreme position**, the **potential energy increases** because the height of the bob increases relative to the lowest point. At the extreme position, the pendulum has maximum potential energy. • As the pendulum moves away from the mean position, its **kinetic energy decreases**. This is because the speed of the pendulum reduces as it approaches the extreme position due to the conversion of kinetic energy into potential energy. • At the mean position, the pendulum has **maximum kinetic energy** and minimum potential energy, as it moves the fastest at this point. • At the extreme position, the pendulum comes to a momentary halt, thus having **zero kinetic energy** and maximum potential energy. • This energy transformation follows the principle of conservation of energy, where the **total mechanical energy** (sum of kinetic and potential energies) remains constant throughout the motion.
